Estimate 2.5% zakat on eligible net assets above nisab. This free online zakat calculator gives you an instant answer without an account, a download or sending your entries to a server. It is designed for quick everyday use on desktop and mobile. This guide explains how to use it, the formula it applies, and a worked example you can follow with your own numbers.

## How to use the Zakat Calculator

Start by entering your cash, savings, gold and investments, then entering your short-term debts to deduct and finally entering your nisab threshold. The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause. When you want a clean slate, Reset restores the defaults.

1. Enter your cash, savings, gold and investments.
2. Enter your short-term debts to deduct.
3. Enter your nisab threshold.
4. Check the result — it updates instantly as you type.
5. Use Reset to start over with the default values.

## Formula

Zakat = 2.5% of eligible net assets when they meet or exceed nisab. Rules vary by asset and scholarly interpretation.

That is the standard formula for this calculation, and it is the same one the [Zakat Calculator](/zakat-calculator) applies to the values you enter. You can work it out by hand, but the calculator is faster when you want to try several values, and it removes the risk of a slip in the arithmetic. If the figures look wrong, check your inputs first — a misplaced decimal point is the usual culprit.

Here is a typical example. 10,000 assets less 1,000 debt leaves 9,000; zakat at 2.5% is 225. The steps are the same whatever numbers you use; only the figures change.
